entries.rationale: Left/right, lighter traffic and center-line distinctions remain separate; the teaching explains opposing-flow predictability rather than inventing a new legal exception.
Signalling before movement remains distinct from after-the-line or move-first distractors and hazard lights; signals supplement the safety check.
Stopping space is preserved as the purpose of the gap; excluding others, abandoning observation and controlling the lead vehicle remain the three actual misconceptions.
Readiness to stop near children remains distinct from waiting for a child in the lane, horn-only travel and close following; no guaranteed child behavior is asserted.
The maximum is not a required target; fastest-vehicle imitation and accelerating out of difficult conditions remain incorrect without adding a numerical limit.
Incomplete mirror coverage, a possibly hidden adjacent vehicle, signals not removing blind spots and reversing-only error are all faithfully retained.
Increasing rear space remains the remedy; sheltering close, blindly following and flashing without increasing the gap remain actual distractors.
The question asks for the position to avoid: close left-side truck exposure remains the hazardous choice, while the three separation/observation alternatives are not mislabelled unsafe.
Turning/reversing sweep and the temporary side gap remain distinct from safe clearance; both translations explain squeezing without prescribing a new maneuver.
The truck may need more stopping distance, not always less; reliance on obligatory truck braking and no-clearance assumptions remain wrong.
Continuous nighttime headlighting remains distinct from waiting for traffic, hazard-light substitution and switching off on an apparently empty road.
Changing to low beam to avoid glare remains conditional; priority demands, repeated flashing and directing light into mirrors remain the actual distractors.
Night reaction/stopping margin remains the reason for distance; brake-light failure, universal priority and replacing the learners own lights are accurately rejected.
Wet-condition speed reduction is preserved; engine operation, pressure from following traffic and accelerating toward dry road do not replace grip considerations.
The wet gap must increase; tracking closely, assuming equal wetness cancels the margin and looking through a rear window remain incorrect.
Smooth planned braking remains distinct from last-moment braking, alternating hard forces and waiting until close behind; skid reasoning is qualitative.
Normal headlights/direction signals remain distinct from continuous hazards, removing headlights and claiming priority with both indicators.
Speed reduction before the bend and lane retention remain the answer; overtaking before limited sight, crossing the center and abrupt mid-bend braking remain unsafe.
A safe parked stop is preserved; hiding the phone, slow travel and a straight road do not remove distraction. The Russian explanation faithfully retains the source conversation wording.
Alternative transport remains the answer after alcohol; slower travel, route familiarity and fresh air do not cancel impairment. No threshold or medical remedy is introduced.
Not driving with impaired alertness is preserved; prescription status, loud music and racing fatigue remain false protections without adding medical advice.
Keeping the sidewalk for pedestrians remains the answer; apparent emptiness, horn use and stationary traffic do not change its purpose.
The shoulder remains available for emergencies rather than ordinary queue bypass; a queue, hazard lights and waiting for an emergency arrival are not permissions.
A stable position inside a lane is preserved; divider occupation, repeated crossing to obstruct overtaking and a light-traffic exception remain distinct errors.
An immediate necessary warning remains the purpose of the horn; punishment, pressure on safe pedestrians and general queue frustration are accurately distinguished.
Slowing and safely keeping left remain the response to oncoming traffic; speed, shared-center occupation and forcing priority to the right remain wrong.
Stopping until a permitting signal remains the answer; an empty-looking junction, following another vehicle and sounding the horn do not permit red-signal travel.
The explicit ability to stop safely is retained; racing red, yellow-as-priority and an added overtake remain incorrect. No unconditional emergency stop is introduced.
Circulating traffic retains priority in this supplied scenario; entering vehicles behind, reversed priority and vehicle size remain actual misconceptions.
The designated circulating path remains the answer; crossing the central area, weaving to shorten travel and reversing direction for a nearby exit remain incorrect.
Stopping for the person already crossing remains the answer; horn/acceleration in front and passing an unchecked stopped vehicle remain distinct distractors.
Parking away from the crossing remains the answer; staying nearby, hazard lights and forcing pedestrians around the vehicle do not excuse obstruction.
Keeping access clear remains the answer; a brief stay, telephone number and closed gate do not establish permission. No new property-law clause is asserted.
A safe move left or stop as needed remains conditional; blocking predictably, exploiting the emergency passage and close following remain wrong.
Waiting clear of the tracks remains the answer; racing the train, leaving a wheel on the rail and bypassing a barrier remain actual unsafe alternatives.
No warning signal triggers additional observation, not an assumption of no train; speed and delegation to a preceding driver remain the wrong shortcuts.
Advance signalling and enough clearance for the complete pass remain necessary; preferred speed, being seen and a horn do not establish a right to overtake.
Allowing space without racing remains the answer; acceleration, crowding and matching speed keep the overtaker exposed rather than completing the maneuver.
Both stopping and parking remain prohibited by the supplied red-white curb guidance; motorcycle, running-engine and long-term-parking exceptions are not invented.
The current posted limit remains the answer; an old road limit, another drivers speed and engine size do not replace the sign. No numerical limit is added.

Fastening before departure remains required by the scenario regardless of short/quiet travel; postponement and airbag substitution remain distinct distractors. The safety note describes restraint, not a legal penalty.
Repair before road use remains the answer; an annual tax date, daylight and carrying a triangle do not cure defective equipment.
Photographing and recording existing rental damage before leaving remains the answer; universal coverage, late reporting and concealment are rejected without inventing an insurance entitlement.
Brake lights warn following drivers; they neither replace following distance, create intersection priority nor indicate turn direction.

The mirror-check, advance left signal and gentle slowdown sequence is preserved; late signals, post-stop observation and brake-light substitution remain incorrect.
The bicycle path and blind spots must be checked; forward-only observation, horn pressure and expecting cyclists to swerve remain the actual distractors.
Waiting enough time for the elderly pedestrian remains the answer; repeated horn, creeping close and driving around the person all pressure or encroach on the crossing.
